claims.text: Pre-coating tungsten particles with an ultra-thin, compositionally graded carbide or nitride interlayer by ALD will improve copper wettability.
The ALD interlayer will promote a void-free and uniform W–Cu interface.
The ALD interlayer will produce a durable W–Cu interface relative to vapor-coated powder sintering.
Discrete tungsten particles or interconnected tungsten regions embedded in copper are typical precursors produced by vapor-coated powder sintering or spark-plasma sintering.
A tungsten carbide or nitride layer can act as a chemical and structural bridge between tungsten and copper.
The conformal ALD coating reduces interfacial energy barriers between tungsten and copper.
Reducing the interfacial energy barrier suppresses void formation.
Changing tungsten surface chemistry with the interlayer enhances copper wetting and promotes full interfacial contact during consolidation.
Improved interfacial contact minimizes phase separation and voids.
Minimizing phase separation and voids creates uniform thermal paths.
Uniform, low-void interfaces improve mechanical durability under irradiation-induced stresses.
Relative to vapor-coated powder sintering, the ALD-treated composite will have less interfacial void formation.
Relative to vapor-coated powder sintering, the ALD-treated composite will have improved thermal transport.
Relative to vapor-coated powder sintering, the ALD-treated composite will retain more mechanical strength under irradiation and thermal cycling.
Vapor-coated tungsten powders can be sintered to yield near-perfect W–Cu interfacial contact.
The long-term performance of vapor-coated W–Cu material under extreme reactor conditions is uncertain.
Consolidation must occur below the tungsten melting temperature and copper boiling temperature.
The treated composite must retain performance under high heat flux, thermal cycling, and irradiation.
The long-term irradiation stability of the ultra-thin ALD interlayer is unknown.
The optimal composition and thickness of the ALD interlayer remain undetermined.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as already yielding near-perfect interfacial contact, while the predicted advantage is reduced interfacial void formation. This is not strictly impossible, but it leaves little clearly defined room for improvement and no baseline defect level is specified.
